# Stress Corrosion Cracking of Aluminum Alloys

## Abstract

This comprehensive analysis examines stress corrosion cracking (SCC) in aluminum alloys, focusing on the mechanisms, susceptibility factors, and behavior across different alloy series. The study reveals that alloys 7079-T6, 7075-T6, and 2024-T3 account for over 90% of service failures in high-strength aluminum alloys. The article explores how metallurgical, environmental, and mechanical factors influence SCC development, with particular attention to the electrochemical theory of stress corrosion. Detailed analysis of various aluminum alloy series (2xxx, 5xxx, 6xxx, 7xxx, and casting alloys) provides insights into their specific SCC resistance characteristics and practical applications.
